units.title: Statement: day 1 settlement (ref GLS-KH-0001-D01)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Statement. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-D01. Period: contract day 1. Status: settlement recorded. Liabilities raised, payments made and any balance carried forward are itemised on the wages page of your Journal, which is the authoritative record. Next statement: contract day 3. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Day report received
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Thanks for the day report. I won't pretend I read every line, but I read the important ones. Quick reminders:
- Supply boat runs are posted on the harbour office board in Gilliver as well as on your supplier page.
- The client would prefer the site stays off social media. No photos online, please.
- Day two is usually when people find out which boots are the wrong boots.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Correction: Accounts
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: A correction to yesterday's note: Accounts are on the third floor, not the second. They moved in the summer and nobody told me, which tells you something about the third floor. Receipts are still essential. Everything else in that note stands, including the part about not replying to Payroll. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: If something urgent comes up
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: If you ever need something from the mainland that genuinely can't wait for the supplier, put it at the top of the day report and mark it urgent. I'll ring the harbourmaster at Gilliver, who is very helpful and knows the boat's skipper. She is not a courier service, though, so please keep it for real emergencies: injuries, broken safety gear, that kind of thing. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A warm welcome from Ardent Vale
units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: Dear colleague, on behalf of everyone at Ardent Vale, welcome to Kittering Holm. We are proud to be beginning a new chapter for the island, guided by our long-term vision and by a deep respect for the Sound and its communities. We are grateful to Grieve Land Services, and to you, for helping us take this important first step together.

units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: As a patient and responsible owner, we believe stewardship means taking the time to do things properly. We have no plans to announce at this time, and we kindly ask that any questions about the island's future are directed to our community desk rather than answered on site. Please do not feel under any pressure to engage with such questions.

units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: We wish you and your colleagues a safe and productive stay. Should you have any thoughts you would like to share, please know that our community desk is always listening. With warm regards, Ardent Vale Community Information. This message was sent from an address that cannot accept replies.

units.title: Trade journal piece today
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: The Timber & Land Trade Journal is running a piece about the contract today. Head office gave them a quote, which I've seen, and which manages to say nothing at all, beautifully. If anybody tries to contact you about the job, they shouldn't be able to, but if they do, please refer them to the office. Not because there's anything to say. It's just tidier. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Burning: condition 4
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: A small one. The planning conditions include fire safety: burning is permitted in the one approved pit only, attended during working hours. Please don't let anyone get creative with a second fire 'to speed things up'. It's condition 4, the council does read these things eventually, and on a clear day the Holm can be seen from half the coast, including by people with telescopes and opinions. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Just checking where we are on numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Just checking where we are on numbers. Not chasing: I need a rough figure for the directors' end-of-week sheet, and whatever the day report says is fine. If the first days are slow, that's normal; most crews find their rhythm by day four or five, once the yard and the lanes are sorted. Thirty days sounds like a lot until it's twenty. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Why don't trees use computers? (Scared of logging in.)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Saw the trade rag. 'Large but straightforward.' I've written that exact sentence myself, about a job where we lost a digger in a bog for a week. Not saying anything. Just saying. Road job update: we found an old well under the hedge, which explains the man, who it turns out was guarding it. He's very relieved. So am I. Hal

units.title: Re: boots
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Forgot to say. If anyone on your crew turned up in new boots, make them swap into their old ones for the first week, blisters or not. New boots on wet roots is how I lost a summer once. Also, if the camp has a dog, and Grieve camps usually seem to end up with a dog, don't let anyone feed it sausages. That's two pieces of wisdom for free. Hal

units.title: rehearsal report
units.author: sam
units.text: rehearsal report. 'the river is rising!' was delivered with enormous feeling, arms up, the lot. then Jamie stepped backwards off the stage block, which was not in the script, and the whole reed section went down like dominoes. nobody hurt. Mrs Okafor, who is directing, said 'that was very naturalistic' through her teeth. we have three more weeks of this. I am going to need a stronger kettle.

units.author: sam
units.text: anyway mum. she's decided the physio is 'too young to understand hips', which is a new one. she's doing the exercises though, I've caught her at it in the kitchen holding onto the fridge like it's a ballet barre. and Pilot has started sleeping on your old jacket by the back door. I haven't the heart to move it. he looks up every time a car goes past.

units.title: saw your island in the paper
units.author: sam
units.text: ps the Courier had a bit about your island yesterday. it said the whole thing is coming down, every tree, in a month?? I read it out to mum and she said 'well, they'll want to get a move on'. it sounds enormous. I hope they're paying you properly. you're allowed to be tired, you know, you don't have to be the one who's never tired.

units.author: sam
units.text: also I looked at the map and your island is the green bit off Gilliver that we used to see from the ferry when we went to Auntie Jo's, the one dad called 'the hedgehog'. I didn't know anyone was allowed on it. anyway I'm rambling, it's late and the library had a school group in today and I can still hear them. love, S x

units.title: Sorry to write out of the blue
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm so sorry to write to you out of the blue. I got this address from the Grieve office when I rang to check that Tomas had got there all right. I'm his sister, Ana. He told me his phone barely works out there, so I thought this might be easier than waiting for him to find a signal. If you get a minute, could you tell him I'm fine, the cat is fine, and he doesn't need to ring.

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: He worries about everything, and it's my job to tell him not to. He doesn't sleep well in new places, so if he looks tired the first week, that's why, it isn't the work. Is he sleeping? Sorry, you don't have to answer that. I know you're busy and this isn't your job. Thank you for reading. Ana

units.title: Grieve Land Services takes on thirty-day island clearance
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Port Ammet contractor Grieve Land Services has begun what it describes as the largest single-site clearance in its history: the felling of every tree on Kittering Holm, a six-kilometre island in the Marrow Sound, within thirty working days. The work began this week from a temporary camp at the island's landing.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The contract, awarded by the island's owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, pays a fixed rate per tree delivered to an on-site yard, with a separate day rate for crew. The Journal understands that timber will be burned on site under the planning conditions rather than shipped, which is now common for island work, where haulage would cost more than the timber is worth.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: A site lead and a small felling crew are working from the camp, supplied by boat from Gilliver. Grieve would not confirm crew numbers or the expected tree count. 'It's large but straightforward,' a company spokesperson said. 'Good people, a clear scope and a fixed timetable. That's all any of us want from a contract.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Thirty days is ambitious for a site of that size. One contractor who has worked island clearances in the north told the Journal that crews typically allow sixty to ninety days for comparable acreage, and that weather is the usual problem. 'Wind, mostly. You can't fell in a gale, and you can't burn in one either. Fog slows you down more than people think.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Ardent Vale, a private holding company, has not disclosed its plans for the island, which it bought eighteen months ago through an intermediary. A statement provided to the Journal said the company was 'proud to be taking a patient, long-term approach' and 'grateful to its partners'. It did not say what the approach was towards.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve has carried out a number of large clearances in the region and further north, mostly for forestry estates and utility corridors. Asked whether the firm had worked on island sites before, the spokesperson said client confidentiality applied 'as it always does', and declined to list previous contracts.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir back to normal after dry summer
units.author: courier
units.text: Brackwater reservoir has returned to its normal level for the time of year after a dry summer left the old road bridge visible for the first time in a decade. The water company said recent rain had refilled the reservoir more quickly than expected, and that the hosepipe advice issued in August has been withdrawn.

units.author: courier
units.text: The low water drew visitors from across the district to photograph the bridge and the foundations of cottages flooded when the dam was built. The estate's ranger said the attention had been welcome but 'wearing', with cars parked on verges and people walking the shoreline long after the paths officially close.

units.author: courier
units.text: Walkers are reminded that the reservoir woods paths close at dusk and that the gates at the dam end are locked overnight. 'People think it's to spoil their fun,' the ranger said. 'It's because the banks are steep, the water's cold, and nobody can hear you shout from the road.'

units.title: Tollinby primary rehearses first full production in five years
units.author: courier
units.text: Pupils at Tollinby primary school are rehearsing their first full-length production in five years, a musical version of the local folk tale The Kingfisher and the King. More than sixty children are taking part, including a chorus of reeds, bulrushes and river stones, and a king played, by popular vote, by a nine-year-old who can whistle.

units.author: courier
units.text: The school's director of the production said the costumes were being made by parents and grandparents at weekly sessions in the church hall. 'We have a lot of green fabric,' she said. 'A great deal of green fabric. If anyone has any blue, we would love to hear from them, because the river is currently very green.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Performances will be held in the school hall over two evenings later in the month. Tickets are free but must be collected in advance from the school office or from the bookshop on the market place, which has agreed to hold them behind the counter 'next to the poetry, where they'll be safe'.

units.title: Council promises replacement recycling lorry 'within weeks'
units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council has said a replacement recycling lorry will be in service 'within weeks', after residents in parts of Port Ammet reported missed collections over most of the past month. The council said the old vehicle failed its inspection and that a hired replacement was too wide for several older streets.

units.author: courier
units.text: Among the streets affected is Rope Walk, where the hired lorry has been unable to make the turn at the chapel end. One resident, a retired postman, said he had reported the missed collection three times and had kept a written record of each call, including how long he spent on hold.

units.author: courier
units.text: Until the new vehicle arrives, the affected streets will be collected on Thursdays by a smaller van. The council asked residents to keep recycling indoors where possible between collections, as gulls have been 'extremely active' in the market area.

units.title: Free ferry passes for Lisle sixth-formers to continue
units.author: courier
units.text: Students from Lisle who travel to the sixth-form college in Port Ammet will keep their free ferry passes for another year, the council has confirmed, after a consultation found the scheme was used by almost every eligible student. The passes cover the first crossing in the morning and the last before seven in the evening.

units.author: courier
units.text: A former teacher at Lisle's primary school, who taught many of the current students, welcomed the decision. 'Half of them would never have stayed on otherwise,' she said. 'You can't revise for exams on a fishing boat, though one or two have tried.' The scheme costs the council a little under forty thousand dollars a year.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines said it would keep a section of the upper lounge for students on the morning crossing during the exam season. The company also confirmed that the coffee machine on the upper deck was 'now operational', a claim the Courier has not independently verified.

units.title: Travel live: the drive home
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 16:30 Good afternoon. The Port Ammet ring road is slow from the college roundabout to the ferry terminal as the school traffic meets the 16:45 crossing traffic. The Brackwater junction lights are behaving. That sentence may age badly.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 17:00 A lorry has shed part of its load of straw bales on the Tollinby road just past the old mill. Nobody is hurt and the farmer is on the scene with a tractor and, we're told, some strong opinions. Expect delays in both directions for about half an hour.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 17:40 The Tollinby road is clear again; the straw is back on the lorry or, in some cases, in the hedge. Sound Lines crossings are running to time. Sea conditions on the Sound are calm, with the Met Office mentioning the possibility of mist later in the week.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:10 A listener has asked us to mention Pebble, a small grey cat with one white sock on her front left paw, missing from Tanners Lane in Port Ammet since this morning. Pebble is friendly but shy. If you have a shed or garage nearby, please have a look before you lock up tonight.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:30 That's the drive home from us. Roads are quiet, the late crossings are on time, and the temperature is dropping fast under clear skies, so watch for frost on the bridges inland after midnight, particularly the reservoir bridge at Brackwater.

units.title: Brackwater substation inspection this week
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound Power Co-op says engineers will carry out a routine inspection of the Brackwater substation over the next few days. The co-op does not expect any interruption to supplies, but says customers in Brackwater and along the Gilliver feeder may notice brief flickers if equipment has to be switched during the work.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The substation, built in the 1960s alongside the reservoir dam, supplies most of the coastal villages between Brackwater and Gilliver. The co-op said the inspection was part of its normal winter preparations and was 'nothing to be concerned about'.

units.title: Distribution park to add 200 seasonal jobs
units.author: weypost
units.text: The distribution park outside Weyhaven is recruiting two hundred seasonal workers ahead of the winter peak, most of them on night shifts. The operator said the roles would run until the new year, with some made permanent. Recruitment days will be held at the park's main gate and at the city library.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Current staff have mixed views. One picker, who asked not to be named, said the work was 'fine if you like walking and being timed while you do it'. Another said the night shift was 'the best-kept secret in the city: quiet, warm, and nobody asks you how your day was'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The extra night workers are one reason the bus company agreed to add a late service on the estuary road from next month. Union representatives have asked that the park's yard floodlights, which cut out during a power dip last winter, be put on a backup supply before the peak begins.

units.title: Night closures for estuary road resurfacing
units.author: weypost
units.text: The estuary road between the container berth roundabout and the Dellow Court junction will close overnight for resurfacing over the next fortnight. Closures will run from 20:00 to 06:00, with a signed diversion through the old dock streets. Buses will continue to serve the Dellow Court stop from the diverted route.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of the tower blocks along the road have been warned to expect noise from the planing machines, which the city council described as 'unavoidable but temporary'. A resident of a third-floor flat said she had heard that before, 'about the lift'.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast: today and tonight
units.author: met
units.text: Today: a grey start with light drizzle in the west, clearing by midday to bright spells. Wind westerly force 2 to 3. Maximum 10°C. Tonight: clear skies and light winds. Frost inland, with temperatures falling to minus 1°C at Brackwater and 2°C on the coast. Visibility good, becoming moderate towards dawn.

units.title: Tides: Gilliver
units.author: met
units.text: High water Gilliver 05:31 (4.2 m) and 17:52 (4.4 m). Low water 11:44 (0.8 m). Times are Sound Time. Spring tides later in the week; slipway users are reminded that the bottom of the Gilliver slip is covered with weed and very slippery near low water.

units.title: Sound Lines: lost property
units.author: ferry
units.text: Lost property handed in on board this week includes three umbrellas, a child's school jumper (Lisle primary, name tape partly removed), a set of house keys on a fish-shaped keyring and a library book about knots. Items may be collected from the Port Ammet terminal office between 09:00 and 16:00.

units.title: Inshore waters: Carrow Point to Weyhaven
units.author: met
units.text: Wind west or southwest 2 to 3, becoming variable 2. Sea state smooth or slight. Weather fair. Visibility good, becoming moderate in mist patches towards dawn. Outlook: light winds persisting, with mist and fog becoming widespread over the Sound from the middle of the week.

units.author: coast
units.text: Further to the earlier notice, the Lisle Spit east cardinal buoy has been restored to its charted position and is showing its correct light characteristic. The earlier notice is cancelled. Mariners are thanked for their reports.

units.title: Lisle west: short interruption
units.author: power
units.text: Customers in Lisle west, including the pier and the school, lost supply for twenty-two minutes from 08:12 after a fault on a pole-mounted transformer. Supplies were restored by switching. Engineers will replace the transformer fuse during the day; no further interruption is expected.

units.title: Brackwater substation: routine inspection
units.author: power
units.text: Routine inspection and maintenance at Brackwater substation will take place over the coming days. No planned interruptions. Customers on the Brackwater and Gilliver circuits may notice brief flickers during switching operations. Please treat all equipment as live and report any damage to the fault line.

units.title: Water main flushing: Gilliver
units.author: council
units.text: The water main serving Gilliver harbour and Quay Row will be flushed between 10:00 and 14:00. Customers may notice discoloured water or reduced pressure during this time. Run the cold tap for a few minutes until the water clears. The water is safe to drink. Please avoid doing laundry until it runs clear.

units.title: Garden waste: last collections of the season
units.author: council
units.text: Garden waste collections will continue fortnightly until the end of next month and then pause for the winter. Please do not put food waste, soil or rubble in the green bins. Bags left beside the bin will not be collected. Festive trees, when the time comes, have their own collection scheme.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Gilliver slipway lights defective
units.author: coast
units.text: Mariners are advised that four of the six shore lights marking the Gilliver slipway are reported unlit. The harbour authority has arranged repairs. Until restored, vessels approaching the slipway during darkness should do so with caution and use their own illumination.

units.title: Sound Lines: late crossing, minor delay
units.author: ferry
units.text: The 19:30 departure from Port Ammet is running approximately ten minutes late following a delay in loading a refrigerated vehicle. Onward Lisle and Gilliver times will be adjusted accordingly. We apologise for the inconvenience.

units.title: Evening update
units.author: met
units.text: A clear, still night. Frost forming quickly inland after dark, especially in the Brackwater valley, where minus 2°C is possible by dawn. Mist patches may form over the reservoir and low ground. Coastal areas staying just above freezing. No warnings in force.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Oct 18th. Tally this week, 268. Best week yet. The men are pleased with the bunkhouse and say the Holm is a dry place for timber. Dobbs had a tooth drawn by Hargreave with the farrier's pincers and has spoke of nothing else. Wages paid in full, £24 15s, entered. Lamp oil used, one barrel near enough, which is more than I allowed for.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Oct 25th. Tally this week, 241, the wind being against us two days. The men keep the bunkhouse lamp burning the whole night through, which I have told them is a waste of oil and of the Company's money. Burrows says it is for the horses. The horses are in the lean-to and cannot see it. Put in for two more barrels.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch, 17 Nov 1904. 00:00 Lamp lit, burning well. Wind N 2, clear, sharp frost, visibility 12 miles. 01:30 Light of a cart moving on the shore road toward Gilliver, presumed the carrier late. 02:00 Trimmed wicks. 04:00 Relieved. Remarks: frost on the lantern glazing, cleared twice.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch, 18 Nov 1904. 00:00 Lamp burning well. Wind NE 3, cloud increasing, visibility 9 miles. 02:15 Fog bell tested, in order. 03:00 Weather closing in from seaward. 04:00 Relieved by assistant keeper. Remarks: assistant keeper's wife unwell; he asks leave to go to Gilliver for the doctor at first light. Granted.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Outer islands, 3 June. Mr. P. on time, sober, offended when I remarked upon it. Puffins on the north stack, perhaps forty; razorbills; a great many kittiwakes and a great deal of noise. One grey seal hauled out, unbothered by me or by Mr. P.'s singing. Ashore on the larger island: rabbits everywhere, the turf grazed like a lawn. [Sketch: rabbit skull, side view.]

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 4 June. Rain all day; stayed at the inn at Gilliver and wrote up. The landlady says no one will take me to the Holm for more than a day, as the boatmen 'like their own beds'. Have offered Mr. P. double. He has said he will think about it, which in Gilliver appears to be a complete sentence.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Jan 15. Blowing hard, no fishing. Went down the harbour with Father to see to the moorings. Mr. Coyle from the curing station come by and says the Holm sheds want new slates before the season and will Father take him over with the slates when the wind drops. Father said aye for the right money. Mother's cough better.

units.title: From the archive: the first car ferry, 1957
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: from the Courier of 4 April 1957, front page. The photograph that accompanied it shows the mayor with one foot on the ramp, which he is said to have refused to take off until the picture was taken. 'The new vehicle ferry between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver entered service on Tuesday, carrying eleven motor cars, a lorry of potatoes and a great many interested persons.'

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: Our Gilliver Correspondent, November 1894. The timber boat makes its weekly passage to the Holm with great regularity, and its master reports the woodmen in good health and better appetite. The candle question has been resolved by Mrs. Tull, who has laid in a gross and raised her price by a farthing, which the village has borne with fortitude. The herring have at last arrived.

units.title: LB-0201: Brackwater Woods, tawny owls, winter night
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0201. Date: 12 December 1988. Location: Brackwater Woods, west of the reservoir path. Kit: portable reel-to-reel, single dynamic mic, no windshield. Duration: 31:40. Description: a male and female tawny owl calling and answering, roughly 40 m apart; a vehicle on the dam road at 18:02; frost crackle in leaf litter throughout. Donated by R. N. (Tollinby).

units.title: LB-0233: Weyhaven fish market, closing time
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0233. Date: 3 March 1996. Location: Weyhaven fish market, main hall. Kit: portable cassette recorder, clip mic on the recordist's collar. Duration: 14:12. Description: hosing of the floor; crates stacked; two traders arguing about a van; a radio playing a football result. Curator's note: the recordist's coat rustles throughout, which several listeners have found 'oddly comforting'.

units.title: Brackwater Reservoir
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Brackwater Reservoir was created in 1968 by damming the Brack valley above the village. Eleven cottages and a road bridge were submerged; the bridge is exposed in very dry years. The substation beside the dam supplies most of the coastal villages to the east. The woods on the western shore are managed by the Brackwater estate. Recordings made in the woods are held by LowBand [citation needed].

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: And the curing station, after the timber men? A: Oh, that was later, that was when I was married. The men went over for the season and came back on the Saturday boat. Q: Did they stay overnight? A: They had huts, the station men. Some stayed. My husband never would. Q: Why was that? A: [long pause] He said the huts were damp. He liked his own bed. You'll have heard that a lot.
